seoTitle: DOI Extractor and doi.org Link Builder
metaDescription: Find DOIs in text or a reference list, clean them and build doi.org links. Checks the pattern only, nothing is looked up. Free, private.
intro: Find DOIs in pasted text or a reference list, clean them up and build doi.org links. Checks the syntax only; it does not look anything up.
why:
Reference lists mix DOIs written as doi:10..., full URLs and bare numbers, often with a full stop stuck on the end.

Paste the text and the tool pulls out each DOI, removes trailing punctuation, drops duplicates and builds a doi.org link. It checks the pattern recommended by Crossref and flags odd characters. It does not look a DOI up: fetching the title and authors needs a request to a server, which this offline tool does not make.
howTo: Paste text or a reference list.
Read the table of DOIs and links.
Check any flagged DOIs by hand.
Use the Citation Generator to format a reference.

faq.q: Does it check the DOI exists?
faq.a: No. It checks the pattern. Opening the link tells you if it resolves.
No, but they are shown as found.
10., four to nine digits, a slash, then letters, digits and some punctuation.
